subject: human eye
title: What If You Never Went Outside?

scenes.text: What if you never went outside again? Your eyes would slowly change shape.
Daylight makes your eye release dopamine, which seems to slow the eyeball from stretching.
Indoors all day, a growing eye stretches longer. Far things blur. That's nearsightedness.
In the US, 42 percent of people are now nearsighted, up from 25 percent in the 1970s.
In Taiwan, about 90 percent of teens were by the end of school. So from 2010, kids were sent outside two hours a day.
By 2015, nearsightedness among young pupils had dropped from 50 percent to 45. Sunny or cloudy, outside counts.

description:
What if you never went outside? Outdoor light is thought to trigger dopamine release in the eye, which slows the eyeball from stretching, and a stretched eye is a nearsighted one.
In the US, 42% of people are now myopic, up from 25% in the 1970s; in Taiwan about 90% of teens are by the end of high school. After Taiwan encouraged two hours of outdoor time a day from 2010, myopia among elementary students fell from a high of 50% in 2011 to 45.1% in 2015.
